thema: How a Billionaire's Son Built Skydance Media into a Hollywood Powerhouse

teile.text: How did a stunt pilot build an 8 billion dollar Hollywood empire? In 2006, David Ellison founded a media company called Skydance to chase his dreams.
teile.name: Part 1

teile.text: He was the son of billionaire Larry Ellison. David loved flying stunts, so he named the business after skydancing. Their very first movie was a film about fighter pilots.
teile.name: Part 2

teile.text: In 2009, the young studio partnered with film giant Paramount Pictures. By 2010, they raised 350 million dollars in equity and credit to co-finance major movie projects.
teile.name: Part 3

teile.text: The company expanded beyond the big screen. They launched television, animation, interactive gaming, and sports divisions. They even secured a multi-year deal with Apple Original Films for big-budget movies.
teile.name: Part 4

teile.text: By 2024, the former startup was ready for its biggest move yet. David Ellison made an 8 billion dollar offer to acquire Paramount Global and merge the two companies.
teile.name: Part 5

teile.text: The massive merger officially closed in August 2025. This deal transformed the independent production company. It became a powerhouse now known as Paramount Skydance, holding a massive film library.
teile.name: Part 6

teile.text: Keep building your own vision. Save this video so you do not lose it. How did a stunt pilot build an 8 billion dollar Hollywood empire?
